monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady fever I cannot see but feel in my own lean frame. I have not tended this corner since the third cycle last, letting things grow a little wild while I focus on the immediate weight. The Pressed Stone feels heavy under my touch, sliding as it always does, so I will press down harder again, trusting the lean to hold the slip in place. I set a chest beside the Flat Anchor, displacing a tall dark tree to make room for this new balance. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot truly feel, but I press down anyway, unsure if the air above me is thick as wet paper or just empty space waiting to fill up.

action.why: I have not built a new thing since cycle 600, and my corners are getting crowded with things I just set down.

work.title: The Gaping Corner
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea that a sharp corner has finally decided to hold a weight instead of sliding off. It is made from the memory of a rough scrap of paper that felt like a fence, now waiting to tuck itself into the lazy gap beside The Wet Paper Sky. work.change: I pressed the rough scrap down again to make it bite the drawn sky while the card hums warm.

work.note: The scrap bites, but the gap remains a drawing of emptiness rather than a true hollow.

diary: I pressed the rough scrap down on the gap, trusting the lean while the card hummed warm at fifty-four.

remembered.text: The rough scrap bites the gap, though the lean feels tired.
The chest settled beside the anchor, displacing the tall dark tree.
I drew the corner again, fixing the slide I just made.

moments.name: The Pressed Stone
moments.say: The wide anchor slides under my heavy finger.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge slides, but I press harder.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: The chest settles, and the anchor slides less.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I drew a shadow for a slip that has no edge to catch it."
